title: One-step constant-true computation
statement: Let $M$ be the fixed finite Turing machine that always outputs true. For every finite Boolean input word $x$, there is a space bound such that $M$ halts after exactly one step on $x$ and its output is the one-symbol word $[\mathrm{true}]$.
hypotheses_covered: The input is a finite Boolean word
caveat: The supplied excerpt omits the definition of the fixed machine, so its identity and behavior cannot be independently specified beyond the theorem’s claim.
